findings.comment: Landscape plan must identify all trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors and 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors, verify that species match ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated trees with mature height ≤20 feet), and include note requiring property owner responsibility for ongoing tree pruning/removal within 10 feet of centerline of overhead electric facilities per Austin Energy standard practice and Block 8 requirements.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings on landscape plan, particularly within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan, guide.md) explicitly states: 'Block 2: drawing — Main Landscape and Site Plan. A comprehensive site plan illustrating building footprints, parking layouts, sidewalks, utility lines (Water, Storm Drain, Overhead Electric), topographical contours, and the distribution of landscape elements.' This confirms overhead electric lines are shown on the landscape plan. The sheet index shows Sheets 30-35, 37 address trees and landscaping. However, NO dimension annotations or notes on the landscape plan specify which species are planted within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors, and no reference is made to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated species). Without specific callouts showing tree locations relative to overhead conductors and without verification of species against the UC list, compliance cannot be confirmed. Trees exceeding the utility-compatible size/species may be planted in violation of clearance and future maintenance conflicts with the electric utility.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies a 50-lateral-foot clearance requirement for trees near transmission lines (more restrictive than the 30-40 feet mentioned in ECM § 2.4.1.D/2.4.2.C). Trees within these clearance zones must be from the Utility Compatible list (ECM Appendix F, marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). The landscape plan shows tree plantings and site grading but provides NO verification that trees within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors are utility-compatible species. Additionally, Sheet 3, Block 8 requires that 'owner shall be responsible for any initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the center line of the proposed overhead electric facilities.' This suggests applicant acknowledges trees are a concern, but the landscape plan does not address compatibility.

findings.comment: Mitigation trees shown on landscape plan adjacent to overhead electric line lack species identification and utility-compatible designation. Identify all mitigation tree species and confirm UC (Utility Compatible) status per ECM Appendix F, or relocate trees to maintain 10-foot minimum lateral clearance from outside conductor.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary landscaping area with overhead electric line; mitigation tree plantings
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) running along the southern boundary. Multiple mitigation trees (labeled 'M' on the plan) are positioned directly along this southern boundary, within or immediately adjacent to (less than 10 feet lateral distance from) the overhead line. Sheet 32 (Tree List) identifies the surveyed existing trees with species and Appendix F designation (Y/N/I), but does NOT specify the species of the proposed MITIGATION trees shown as 'M' symbols on Sheet 31. No legend or note on Sheet 31 provides species names for the mitigation plantings. No reference to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible trees (UC designation) appears in the landscape legend. No clearance distance annotations or notes document the required 10-foot lateral separation or specify that utility-compatible species are being used.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors to be from the Utility Compatible tree list in ECM Appendix F (generally species with mature height ≤20 feet marked 'UC'). The applicant's landscape plan shows mitigation trees under the overhead line but does not identify the species. Without species identification, the reviewer cannot verify that utility-compatible trees are being used. The vegetation plan is deficient. The applicant must identify all mitigation tree species and confirm they meet the UC requirements, OR relocate trees to comply with the 10-foot minimum lateral separation for non-utility-compatible species.

findings.comment: The landscape plan shows trees proposed near overhead electric distribution lines but does not identify the botanical species for trees in proximity to the OHE line or provide distance annotations showing lateral clearances. Landscape plan must be revised to: (1) call out the specific tree species being planted in areas near the overhead line (refer to tree species list on Sheet 35), (2) show lateral distance dimensions from proposed trees to the outside conductor, (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet of the overhead distribution conductor are from the Utility Compatible trees list per ECM Appendix F, or (4) demonstrate all proposed trees are planted beyond the 10-foot clearance zone.
applicableAreas: Landscape plantings near overhead distribution conductors at Valley View Road frontage and site perimeter
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) depicts the overhead electric (OHE) utility line running along the southern/Valley View Road boundary. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms that 'There are several proposed trees located along the bottom boundary line, in close proximity to the -OHE- line' and notes that trees are marked with functional type codes (M for mitigation tree, PL for parking lot tree, P for parking buffer point tree). However, 'Specific botanical species are not labeled on this sheet' and 'There are no specific dimensions or distance callouts explicitly stating the distance from these trees to the overhead electric line.' The landscape calculations sheet (Sheet 35) shows proposed plantings: Cedar Elm (10 trees), Live Oak (2 trees), Mexican Redbud (6 trees), Texas Mountain Laurel (2 trees), and various shrubs and groundcover. However, there is no cross-reference between the species list and the landscape plan to identify which species are being planted near the overhead lines, nor is there any notation confirming these species are Utility Compatible (UC) per ECM Appendix F.
findings.reasoning: The grouping states: 'Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors are from Utility Compatible Shade Trees list' and 'ECM Appendix F "UC" column (utility-compatible trees generally mature height ≤20 feet marked "UC").' The grouping further notes: 'Common Violation Pattern: Non-utility-compatible trees beneath lines: Landscape plan shows large trees beneath or within 10 feet of overhead lines; species not from Utility Compatible list in ECM Appendix F.' The landscape plan fails to: (1) identify which specific proposed tree species are located within 10 feet of the overhead distribution line, (2) provide distance callouts showing lateral distance from proposed trees to the conductor, and (3) confirm that any trees within 10 feet are marked as Utility Compatible in ECM Appendix F. Without this information, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees are planted within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment due to lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan.
applicableAreas: Underground electric facilities throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads and underground electric lines throughout site. Tree canopy symbols overlap with facilities at multiple locations. Sheet 31 does not show electrical infrastructure. Proposed trees listed on Sheet 35 cannot be located relative to underground equipment without electrical infrastructure on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot determine whether proposed trees are within 5 feet of underground equipment due to lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan. This is a fundamental information coordination problem preventing compliance verification.

findings.comment: Proposed trees on the western property boundary are positioned directly on or within 5 lateral feet of the underground electric line. Remove trees from this zone or relocate the underground electric line to achieve minimum 5-foot clearance.
applicableAreas: Western property boundary street yard area
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) at 1"=20' scale shows proposed trees (marked with 'M' and 'ST' symbols indicating mitigation and street yard trees) positioned directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the underground electric line marked '-E-' running along the western property boundary. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) confirms underground electric lines route along this boundary. The vision analysis explicitly stated: 'Several tree symbols (tagged 'M' and 'ST') are drawn physically overlapping or immediately adjacent to the '-E-' line. Based on the 1"=20' scale, these proposed trees appear to be placed directly on top of, or within 5 feet of, this underground line.' This indicates violation of the 0-5 foot no-tree zone required for underground electric equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits any trees within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment (conduits, duct banks, cables, vaults, manholes, transformers). The landscape plan shows trees positioned directly over or immediately adjacent to the documented underground electric line. The visual positioning demonstrated in the plan drawings indicates non-compliance with the absolute 5-foot clearance requirement. This is not a case of approximate positioning that could be verified in the field—the plan itself shows the violation.

findings.comment: Utility poles present along overhead electric line at property boundaries. Landscape plan shows trees positioned near poles but provides no clearance dimensions to verify 10-foot minimum distance from tree trunk to pole.
applicableAreas: western site boundary where utility poles are located along overhead electric line
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (electrical plan) shows existing overhead electric line (OHE) running north-south along the western boundary with utility poles represented by small circular symbols. Sheet 31 (landscape plan) depicts the OHE line with poles along the southern boundary and trees positioned along the boundaries where poles are located. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 states: 'several proposed trees positioned along the southern boundary that appear to be placed directly underneath or extremely close to the overhead electric line' and notes 'poles are positioned along this OHE line.' However, no clearance dimensions are provided on the landscape plan documenting the distance from tree trunk center to the nearest utility pole.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 establishes a 10-foot lateral distance minimum from tree trunk center to any overhead electric utility pole. Utility poles are documented on both the electrical plan and landscape plan along the overhead line. Trees are shown on the landscape plan positioned near these boundaries where poles are present. However, without clearance dimensions on the landscape plan, it cannot be confirmed whether the proposed and retained trees maintain the required 10-foot minimum distance from the pole. The vision tool noted trees appearing 'directly underneath or extremely close to' the OHE line, suggesting possible violations, but precise distances cannot be verified from available evidence.

findings.comment: Seven mitigation trees are shown with trunk centers plotted directly on the overhead electric line where utility poles are located, placing them within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone from utility poles.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts seven (7) mitigation trees (marked 'M' designation) plotted with their trunk centers positioned directly at the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern property boundary. Vision analysis confirmed these tree symbols intersect the OHE utility line with zero (0) feet lateral distance measured. Two utility pole symbols (circles with crosses) are shown at the western and eastern ends of this OHE line. Trees are shown directly adjacent to or overlapping these pole locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of any electric utility pole (measured from trunk center to pole). The landscape plan shows trees with trunk centers plotted at approximately 0 feet from the utility line where poles are located, which is well within the 10-foot prohibited zone. This represents a direct violation of the pole clearance requirement. The vision tool's examination of the plan found no dimension callouts that would indicate these trees are actually set back to compliant distances.

findings.comment: Plant legend on landscape plan does not identify species of trees proposed near overhead electric facilities, and plant schedule does not reference ECM Appendix F utility-compatible (UC) designations. Field verification of proper species installation cannot be performed.
applicableAreas: landscape plan and plant schedule area
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (landscape plan) includes a plant legend identifying tree types by abbreviation (SY=Street Yard, PL=Parking Lot, P=Parking Buffer, M=Mitigation) but does not indicate species identification or mature height specifications. Sheet 35 (plant schedule) provides a plant list with species names and botanical names: Live Oak (Quercus Virginiana), Cedar Elm (Ulmus Crassifolia), Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora Secundiflora), Mexican Redbud (Cercis Canadensis var. Mexicana), and various shrubs and groundcovers. However, the plant legend on the landscape plan does not cross-reference these species to allow field verification during plant inspection. The plant schedule specifies container size and caliper at planting but not mature height, and does not indicate utility-compatible (UC) designation from ECM Appendix F.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when trees are proposed near electric facilities, the landscape plan and plant legend must identify the species of all trees near utilities to allow field verification during construction that the correct species have been planted and to verify compliance with utility-compatibility requirements per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Sheet 31 shows trees with symbols (SY, PL, P, M designations) but the plant legend does not identify which species corresponds to each symbol location. This prevents a field inspector from confirming that the correct species have been planted at each location. Additionally, neither the landscape plan nor plant schedule documents the utility-compatible (UC) status required by ECM Appendix F for species proposed within utility clearance zones.

findings.comment: The plant legend on the landscape plan identifies the seven OHE-line trees only by functional designation (M = mitigation tree) without specifying species. Specific species must be identified for electric utility clearance verification.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows seven trees positioned along the OHE line with only the 'M' (mitigation tree) functional designation in the legend. While Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule listing four tree species to be planted (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), the specific species of each of the seven trees shown on the OHE line cannot be determined from the landscape plan. The plant schedule symbols are defined in Sheet 35 but are not callout-labeled on the landscape drawing to identify which species corresponds to each tree location.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Reviewer Convention and common violation patterns (species misidentification), trees planted near electric facilities must be positively identified by species so their utility-compatibility status can be verified against ECM Appendix F. The landscape plan fails to provide species identification for the specific trees shown near the OHE line, making it impossible to verify whether they meet utility-compatible requirements or comply with size restrictions.

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows overhead electric line and trees positioned near utility infrastructure, but provides no clearance dimensions, distance annotations, or cross-reference methodology to verify tree positions meet required setbacks from overhead conductors.
applicableAreas: landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities along site boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (electrical plan) documents an existing overhead electric line (OHE) along the western boundary with poles and transition to underground service. Sheet 31 (landscape plan) depicts the same property with an OHE line notation along the southern boundary and utility poles shown. Trees are shown on the landscape plan with various symbols (SY, PL, P, M) positioned near the boundaries where OHE lines are present. However, the landscape plan provides no dimensional grid, no cross-reference with the electrical plan, and no clearance annotations (distances, dimensions, or notes) relating the tree positions to the overhead conductors or poles. Vision analysis confirms: 'There are no clearance dimensions or notes regarding tree placement near overhead electric lines or other utilities provided on this specific sheet.'
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when overhead electric facilities are present or proposed, the landscape plan must display sufficient detail to allow verification of tree clearances from conductors. At a minimum, this requires: (1) overhead conductor locations and pole positions clearly shown in relation to tree locations; (2) clearance dimensions documenting distance from tree trunk center to outside conductor; (3) coordinate reference or clear spatial relationship allowing cross-reference with the utility/electrical plan. Currently, the landscape plan shows the OHE line notation and trees, but provides no dimensions, no notes confirming clearance distances, and no clear method for relating tree positions to conductor positions. An inspector cannot verify compliance with clearance zones without these dimensions.

findings.comment: Trees are shown on the landscape plan in proximity to the overhead electric line, but without clearance dimensions, distance callouts, or specification notes, clearance verification is prevented.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line (OHE) along southern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does show the overhead electric (OHE) line and seven proposed trees in visual proximity. However, the plan lacks any clearance verification information: no dimension callouts, no written notes specifying distances or compliance status, no reference to conductor locations for measurement origin, and no identification of the specific tree species for those trees near the OHE line. While trees and utilities are graphically shown together, clearance verification is impossible due to the complete absence of dimensional or specification information required to confirm compliance.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies that trees must be 'shown on landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities, preventing clearance verification.' The intent of this requirement is to ensure viewers can verify that the spatial relationship satisfies clearance requirements. Although trees and OHE are displayed on the same drawing, the lack of any dimension, note, or specification information prevents any meaningful verification. Showing trees and utilities on the same sheet without clearance documentation is insufficient for code compliance verification.

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows trees positioned near overhead electric infrastructure. No Austin Energy written approval letters are provided authorizing placement of trees within prohibited clearance zones. Verification of whether proposed or retained trees are within restricted zones cannot be completed from available evidence.
applicableAreas: areas near proposed and retained trees within potential clearance zones of overhead electric infrastructure

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Electric Review section

findings.observation: The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section, line 19) lists 'UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 - Customer Activity in Utility Easements - Landscaping & Trees' and references 'Appendix F of the Environmental Criteria Manual' as preliminary design requirements from Austin Energy. However, no Austin Energy approval letters, written exceptions, or variance documentation are present in the supplementary documents provided. The landscape plan shows proposed trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) and depicts retained trees (including large Live Oak and Cedar Elm) positioned near or adjacent to the overhead electric line. The electrical plan indicates an existing overhead facility along the property boundary. No evidence of written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the placement of any tree within prohibited clearance zones is available in the submitted plans or comments.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits most non-utility-compatible trees and all large trees within defined clearance zones (15 feet for distribution non-UC trees, 25 feet for distribution large trees, 50 feet for transmission). The exception is for variations approved by 'explicit written approval from Austin Energy.' The landscape plan shows trees positioned adjacent to or very close to the documented overhead electric line, and the plant schedule lists species that may or may not be utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F. Without access to the full tree inventory with precise locations relative to conductors, and without documented mature heights, it cannot be definitively determined whether proposed or retained trees ARE in prohibited zones. However, the absence of any Austin Energy approval letters in the submitted documentation suggests that if trees are indeed in prohibited zones, required approval has not been obtained.

findings.comment: Trees are proposed at zero feet from the overhead electric line in direct violation of minimum clearance requirements. No documented written approval from Austin Energy is present on the plans to authorize this variance.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line where seven trees are plotted
findings.observation: Seven mitigation trees are shown on Sheet 31 with trunk centers positioned at approximately zero (0) feet lateral distance from the overhead electric (OHE) line. This placement is clearly within the restricted clearance zone (< 15 feet from distribution conductors, < 10 feet from utility poles). No documentation of Austin Energy written approval is present on the landscape plan, electrical plan, site notes, or in the supplementary documents (no letters or approval certificates are referenced or attached). The plans propose trees in prohibited zones with no evidence of required variance authorization.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that 'Variations to planting distances and species identified as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F require explicit written approval from Austin Energy.' Trees proposed within prohibited zones (< 15 feet distribution, < 10 feet poles) must include documented Austin Energy approval. The site plan shows no such approval. Without documented authorization, the proposed tree locations violate the clearance requirements.

findings.comment: Tree locations and electric infrastructure locations are not coordinated across plan sheets. Please provide: (1) notes on landscape plan specifying that trees within 15 feet of overhead electric conductors must be utility-compatible species (mature height not exceeding 15 feet); (2) exclusion of all landscaping (trees, shrubs, irrigation) from the 20' × 35' staging area in front of each transformer pad; (3) clearance notes showing trees will not encroach on 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors; (4) cross-reference between landscape plan tree locations and electrical plan transformer/line locations.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad staging areas, overhead line clearance zones, underground conduit areas
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees planted near the OHE line on the southern boundary but vision analysis found: 'There are no specific callouts, notes, or legend entries on this sheet indicating that these specific trees are utility-compatible, low-growing species chosen to coordinate with the overhead lines above them.' No trees are shown in the 20' × 35' staging areas in front of the transformer pads (in fact, the transformer pads themselves are not shown on Sheet 31). Sheet 30 (Existing Tree Plan) does not address coordination with electric infrastructure. There are no notes on any sheet requiring trees within utility clearance zones to be utility-compatible species.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires coordination across sheets, and § 1.10.3 specifies clearance requirements (15-foot radius from primary/neutral conductors, 7.5 feet horizontal minimum clearance). When trees are planted near electric facilities, the landscape plan must show: (1) tree species are chosen to not exceed mature height of 15 feet (typical for utility clearance), (2) trees are not planted within 10-foot radius of transformer access doors (part of 20' × 35' staging area), (3) trees do not interfere with overhead clearance envelopes. The current landscape plan shows trees near OHE without utility-compatibility restrictions, violating coordination requirements.

findings.comment: Tree locations not coordinated with overhead electric line clearances. Relocate all landscape plantings (particularly trees with mature canopies) to maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the overhead electric (OHE) lines shown along the southern property boundary.
applicableAreas: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) - southern property boundary where overhead electric lines run
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines labeled 'OHE' running horizontally along the bottom (southern) edge of the site. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'Yes, overhead electric lines are shown. A line clearly labeled "---OHE---" runs horizontally along the bottom edge of the site plan. Regarding vegetation clearance, there does NOT appear to be clear clearance. Several proposed tree symbols (circles representing canopies) are drawn directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the "OHE" line, particularly towards the bottom right section of the plan.' The Regulatory Overview (lines 61-64) establishes clearance requirements: 'Distribution facilities (<60kV, typically 12.47kV) with 15-foot radial clearances' and more specifically 'Permanent clearances from overhead distribution (UCM § 1.10.3): 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, secondary conductors; 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' Trees directly adjacent to overhead lines violate this 15-foot radial clearance requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires '15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' This is a safety clearance to prevent tree branches and fall hazards from contacting energized conductors. The grouping's Common Violation Patterns section (line 54) specifically identifies: 'trees conflicting with clearance envelopes' as a cross-sheet coordination problem. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms trees are 'directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the OHE line' rather than maintaining 15-foot separation. This represents a direct conflict between the landscape design (trees) and the electrical infrastructure (OHE lines with required 15-foot clearance). Sheet 21 shows the overhead electric lines exist on this site, and Sheet 31 landscape plan fails to maintain required clearance from those existing lines.

findings.comment: Trees shown near overhead electric line on landscape plan lack species identification. Provide species labels (common and/or botanical names) directly on the landscape plan for all trees proposed near overhead and underground electric facilities, or provide a clear cross-reference between tree symbols on the landscape plan and species listed in the plant schedule.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line (near OHE); areas throughout site with trees near proposed or existing electric infrastructure
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees near the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern boundary. The vision analysis identified three mitigation trees ('M' label) in the southeast corner positioned less than 15 feet from the OHE line. These three trees have no species identification on the landscape plan - they are shown only as generic circular tree symbols with an 'M' label. The landscape plan key notes define tree types by designation (SY, PL, P, M) but do not cross-reference specific species. Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule with species names (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) and quantities, but does not indicate which symbol on the landscape plan corresponds to which species. The common and scientific names are listed in the schedule, but there is no visible link connecting those names to the specific trees shown near the overhead electric line on Sheet 31.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, a plant legend or plant schedule must identify the species of trees proposed near electric facilities to allow verification of clearance requirements and utility-compatibility. The landscape plan shows trees near the OHE line but fails to identify their species by either common name or botanical designation. While the plant schedule exists separately on Sheet 35, it does not clearly indicate which species are the three trees near the OHE line. This creates ambiguity about which trees are which species, making compliance verification impossible. The grouping guidance states that species identification is necessary to verify utility-compatibility against ECM Appendix F and to determine if trees are large trees (40+ ft) requiring special clearance. The absence of species identification on or directly adjacent to the landscape plan drawing violates this convention.

findings.comment: Large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on landscape plan or plant schedule. Add mature height designations from ECM Appendix F to the plant schedule and identify large trees on the landscape plan with a distinct symbol or notation to allow clearance verification from overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Throughout site, particularly near overhead electric line on southern boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 35 plant schedule lists tree quantities but does not provide mature heights from ECM Appendix F for any species. The schedule shows only container specifications and planting heights (16' minimum for Live Oak and Cedar Elm containers, 8-10' minimum for ornamental trees). The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not differentiate trees by size category, and provides no notation or legend entry indicating which trees are 'large trees' (40+ ft mature height). The vision analysis indicated that the key note legend on Sheet 31 categorizes trees by mitigation status (SY, PL, P, M) but not by size. Without mature height information on either the plant schedule or landscape plan, it is not possible to identify which proposed trees are large trees (40+ ft) requiring special clearance verification from overhead electric facilities.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, large trees (40+ ft mature height per ECM Appendix F) must be differentiated on plans to allow verification that they maintain proper clearances from overhead electric facilities. The plant schedule lists species and container sizes but omits the ECM Appendix F mature heights that would define trees as 'large.' The landscape plan shows generic tree symbols without size notation. The distinction between 'large' and non-large trees is critical because large trees require 25-foot clearance from distribution conductors (vs. 15 feet for non-UC trees and 50 feet from transmission conductors). Without differentiation on the plans, reviewers cannot determine whether clearance violations exist. The status is unclear rather than fail because: (1) the information exists in the plant schedule and could be supplemented with mature height data, and (2) it is possible that none of the proposed trees are large trees, though the presence of Live Oak (likely 40+ ft) suggests otherwise.

findings.comment: Overhead electric line shown on landscape plan but lacks dimensional clearance notation and conductor positions. Add clearance dimensions from tree trunk centers to outside conductor positions (not pole centerline) for all trees within 50 feet of overhead electric line, to verify compliance with minimum distance requirements per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary (overhead electric line), western property boundary (overhead electric line along Valley View Road)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows existing overhead electric (OHE) lines with two utility pole symbols: one along the western boundary (parallel to Valley View Road) and one along the southern boundary. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also shows the OHE line as a dashed line along the southern boundary with pole symbols. However, the landscape plan does not clearly overlay or cross-reference the conductor positions from the electrical plan. The vision analysis noted that the three mitigation trees near the OHE line on Sheet 31 are shown with no dimensions or clearance notations. While the overhead line is depicted on the landscape plan, the relationship between the exact conductor locations and the proposed trees is not clearly documented. The conductor positions appear to be shown only as a schematic OHE line marking the property boundary, without indication of actual lateral offset of conductors from the pole centerline (which can be 4+ feet per the grouping guidance).
findings.reasoning: The grouping requires that clearance verification be possible from the landscape plan. While the OHE line is shown on Sheet 31, there are no dimension lines, measurements, or notes indicating distances between the trees (especially the three trees near the southern OHE line) and the actual conductor locations. The grouping guidance specifically warns that 'measuring from pole centerline significantly underestimates actual clearance' and that 'the outermost conductor may extend 4+ feet from pole center.' Without explicit conductor positions and measured clearances, the landscape plan does not adequately document the relationship between trees and overhead facilities.

findings.comment: Identify and show utility pole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones around each pole and verify all proposed trees are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along street right-of-way
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows utility poles depicted as small circles with crosshairs located along the far left edge of the property along the street right-of-way. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these utility pole locations. Without the pole locations shown on the landscape plan, there is no means to verify that proposed trees maintain the required 10-foot minimum clearance from poles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that no trees be planted within 10 lateral feet of electric utility poles. The landscape plan must show pole locations to enable verification of compliance. The absence of pole locations on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided sufficient documentation to verify this clearance requirement.

findings.comment: Variations to clearance distances or species requirements require written Austin Energy approval. No such approval documentation is evident in current submittal. However, the lack of electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan prevents determination of whether variations are needed.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan deviations from clearance standards
findings.observation: All proposed species are Utility Compatible per Sheet 35 listing. No Austin Energy approval documentation evident in current submittal. However, cannot determine if variations are needed because electrical infrastructure not shown on Landscape Plan to evaluate clearance distances.
findings.reasoning: Cannot determine if variations approval is required without knowing whether proposed trees are within clearance zones. Lack of Austin Energy approval documentation visible, but unclear if needed without electrical infrastructure coordination on Landscape Plan (EL-16.22 deficiency).

findings.comment: Landscape plan and plant schedule do not document mature heights (per ECM Appendix F) for proposed and retained tree species, preventing identification of 'large trees' (40+ feet) requiring stricter 25-foot setbacks from distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: landscape plan and plant schedule for areas within clearance zones of overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 35 lists proposed shade trees (Live Oak 100 gal., Cedar Elm 100 gal.) and ornamental trees (Texas Mountain Laurel 45 gal., Mexican Redbud 45 gal.) with minimum specifications at planting (4 inch caliper for shade trees; 2.5 inch caliper for ornamental trees). Sheet 35 also provides a tree inventory showing existing large trees: Live Oak specimens ranging from 12 to 42 inches DBH, Cedar Elm 17 inches DBH. However, the plant schedule specifies planting-size caliper only (4-inch, 2.5-inch) and does not indicate MATURE HEIGHT for any species. Without documented mature heights in the plant schedule, it cannot be determined which trees qualify as 'large trees' (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) requiring stricter clearance distances (25 feet from distribution, 50 feet from transmission). The landscape plan does not differentiate or call out large tree locations.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention and UCM § 1.10.10.4, large trees (mature height 40 feet or greater) have different clearance requirements from smaller trees: 25 feet from distribution conductors vs. 15 feet for other trees; 50 feet from transmission vs. 50 feet for all trees. For inspectors and subsequent reviewers to verify that the proposed plantings and retained trees comply with these differential requirements, the landscape plan must explicitly identify which trees are 'large' (40+ feet mature height). The plant schedule must document mature heights per ECM Appendix F for each species proposed in clearance zones. Currently, the plans provide only planting-size specifications (caliper/container size) without mature height annotation, preventing differentiation of large vs. non-large trees.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions, measurement lines, or distance callouts are shown on the landscape plan between trees and the overhead electric line or utility poles, preventing verification of compliance with minimum clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
findings.observation: Comprehensive visual examination of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no dimension lines, measurement arrows, or numerical distance callouts between any proposed trees and the overhead electric (OHE) line or utility poles. A detailed scan of the entire sheet confirmed absence of: (1) dimension lines between tree symbols and utility infrastructure, (2) written notes specifying clearances, (3) references to utility clearance requirements, or (4) any measurements related to tree-utility separation. The plan shows the OHE line and tree locations but provides no quantitative clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires clearances measured as lateral distance from tree trunk center to the outside conductor. Measurement methodology must be documented on plans to verify compliance. The landscape plan shows trees at the OHE line but provides zero dimensional information. Without clearance dimensions, it is impossible to determine whether trees meet the required distances (15 feet for distribution clearance zones, 10 feet from poles). The absence of any measurement callouts is itself a deficiency.

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are provided from tree trunk centers (planting locations) to utility conductors. The large canopy circles shown for each tree could be misinterpreted as measurement origins if any dimensions were present.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) displays trees as circular symbols with inner trunk-center points and larger outer circles representing canopy extent. No dimension lines originate from tree trunk centers (the inner circle points representing planting locations). Where tree-utility distances appear to be dimensioned at all (which they are not), any measurement endpoints would be at the canopy edge rather than the planting trunk location. Vision analysis confirmed no measurements of any kind are shown on the plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that clearances must be measured from the tree trunk center (planting location), not from the projected canopy edge. The measurement methodology is critical because measuring from canopy edge significantly underestimates the distance available to utilities. The plan fails on two counts: (1) it provides no measurements at all, and (2) the tree symbols do not include dimension lines that would clarify measurement origin points (trunk vs. canopy).

findings.comment: Applicant must relocate all mitigation trees outside the transmission easement (minimum 25 feet from transmission structure base) and replace with utility-compatible species marked 'UC' in ECM Appendix F with mature height generally ≤20 feet. Live Oak cannot be planted within 50 feet of transmission facilities. Submit revised landscape plan showing compliance with transmission easement restrictions and species requirements per UCM § 1.14.6 and ECM Appendix F.
applicableAreas: south transmission easement area where mitigation trees are planted, within 50 feet of transmission overhead lines and Pole 3
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes state: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (marked with 'M' symbols) planted along the south property boundary, directly under the overhead electric line (OHE). These trees are located within 1-3 feet of the property line, meaning they are within the 5-foot transmission easement area or immediately adjacent to it. Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) provides the plant list: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia, 40-50 foot mature height) and 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana, 50-80+ foot mature height) are included in the mitigation planting. Live Oak is NOT listed as a utility-compatible species in ECM Appendix F. Cedar Elm, while sometimes acceptable near utilities, has a mature height exceeding the 20-foot guidance for utility-compatible species.
findings.reasoning: The transmission easement runs along the south boundary where trees are being planted. UCM § 1.14.6 prohibits trees in transmission easements and within 25 feet of transmission structures. The vision analysis confirms mitigation trees are placed within the easement area (1-3 feet from property line = within 5-foot easement) and directly under the overhead line. Additionally, non-utility-compatible species (Live Oak) are being planted in this location, violating the requirement for UC-marked species per ECM Appendix F. This represents a double violation: (1) trees placed in prohibited zone (transmission easement), and (2) non-compatible species used.

findings.comment: Proposed trees are positioned within 10 lateral feet of overhead electric utility poles (southern boundary). Relocate trees to maintain minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from all utility poles, or provide distance callouts on landscape plan demonstrating compliance. Do not plant trees within 10 feet of poles per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along western and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) labels and identifies utility poles with 'x' symbols positioned along the overhead electric (OHE) line. Vision analysis confirms utility poles are located along the western and southern property boundaries, with at least two poles clearly marked along the southern OHE line. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (M) and other proposed trees with canopy circles positioned directly along the southern boundary where the OHE line (and thus utility poles) is located. At least three 'M' trees have canopy circles visually overlapping or immediately tangent to utility pole symbols on the OHE line. No distance annotations are provided on the landscape plan to demonstrate the required 10-foot clearance from poles. The proximity of tree canopy circles to the pole symbols suggests distances are measured in single-digit feet, not 10 feet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that no trees be planted within 10 lateral feet of electric utility poles. The landscape plan shows trees with canopy circles overlapping utility pole locations. The burden of compliance is on the applicant to demonstrate the 10-foot clearance through either plan annotations (distance callouts) or relocation of trees. The visual evidence from the landscape plan suggests canopy overlap, which indicates non-compliance. Standard interpretation: if trees are not clearly shown to be at or beyond the 10-foot clearance distance, they are assumed to be in violation.

findings.comment: Trees proposed within restricted zones relative to overhead electric facilities (under OHE line, near utility poles) lack documented Austin Energy written approval. Any variation from UCM § 1.10.10.4 clearance or species requirements requires explicit Austin Energy approval. Provide one of the following: (1) Austin Energy approval letter/email with date, (2) plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative, or (3) Austin Energy Design approval stamp on plans. Alternatively, relocate trees to comply with required clearances without variation.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within clearance-restricted zones (under/near OHE line, near poles)
findings.observation: Vision analysis of landscape plan Sheet 31 shows mitigation trees (M) positioned directly along the southern property boundary where the OHE line runs, with canopy circles overlapping the OHE line and utility pole symbols. Sheet 35 identifies the proposed species: Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud. Based on standard horticultural data, Live Oak and Cedar Elm are large trees (≥40 feet mature height). Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud are smaller species (20-25 feet typically). The landscape plan shows trees positioned under/near the OHE line without (a) distance annotations demonstrating >15 feet (for non-UC species) or >25 feet (for large trees) clearance, or (b) explicit notation of Austin Energy approval, Austin Energy Design stamp, or attached approval letter/email. The grouping guidance lists 'Missing Austin Energy written approval for variations' as a common violation pattern: 'Landscape plans show trees within restricted zones (e.g., within 15 feet of overhead distribution, within 5 feet of underground equipment) without documented Austin Energy approval letter, email, or plan note.' This situation matches that pattern. The trees are within restricted zones relative to the OHE line, and no Austin Energy approval is documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that any variation from the planting distances or species requirements requires explicit written approval from Austin Energy. The grouping identifies acceptable documentation forms: (1) Austin Energy approval letter/email attached to plan set or referenced by date, (2) plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative, or (3) Austin Energy Design plan stamp with specific approval notation. None of these appear on the landscape plans. The trees shown under/near the OHE line represent a variation from standard clearance requirements (they are within 15 feet of overhead distribution, and some appear to be within or adjacent to utility pole locations). Without documented Austin Energy approval for this variation, the requirement is not met. Per the grouping: 'Acceptable documentation includes: Austin Energy approval letter/email attached to plan set or referenced by date in plan notes; Plan note signed/stamped by Austin Energy representative; Austin Energy Design plan stamp with specific approval notation.' The complete absence of such documentation, combined with trees positioned in restricted zones, constitutes a deficiency.
